summary: Tenant saw split routing and intermittent fallback after staggered canary weight update
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged canary rollout for redwood-v2-3b-alpha on a dedicated customer tenant (NimbleScribe), partial weight changes were applied by the control-plane replicas out of order. The result was a cohort split: some edge proxies served the new variant while others continued routing to the prior variant, and several sessions observed intermittent fallback to the legacy model.

Impact:
- Affected ~7% of requests for the customer during a 22-minute window.
- Customers reported inconsistent model outputs within the same session (mixed responses).
- Observed increased 5xxs and fallback traffic to legacy variant causing cost and latency spikes.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-11T10:14:00 - Canary weight change initiated (operator request).
- 2026-03-11T10:14:12 - Control-plane replica A accepted and applied weight change.
- 2026-03-11T10:14:19 - Control-plane replica B applied a partial change with older commit index, producing a transient routing table mismatch.
- 2026-03-11T10:36:00 - Support alerted by NimbleScribe (customer ticket).
- 2026-03-11T10:40:00 - Emergency mitigation (temporary explicit model pin via tenant API) applied.

Environment:
- Cluster: dedicated-pool-17 (customer-dedicated).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Edge proxies: ep-us-east-[a,b,c].
- Orchestrator version: 1.18.3.
- Control-plane replicas: 3 (running 1.4.11).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Trigger a staged weight update that increments canary weight in two distinct control-plane transactions.
2. Watch commit propagation when a control-plane replica lags and applies an update with an older commit index.
3. Edge proxies using routing snapshot from lagging replica maintain previous routing for active session tokens; new proxies receive updated snapshot and route to canary variant.
4. When edge reconnects or session token rotates, requests are retried and routed to legacy variant (fallback).

Observed behavior:
- Interleaved responses (session A: first 3 responses from canary, next 2 from legacy).
- Elevated fallback counts in routing metrics (fallback_ratio spike to 0.07).
- KV cache misses increased when switching variants, increasing p99 latency by ~240ms for the tenant.

Expected behavior:
- Atomic cohort-level commit for canary weight changes across control-plane replicas; consistent routing snapshots distributed to all edges before acceptance.

Logs and metrics (selected):
- Orchestrator logs: /var/log/orchestrator/2026-03-11/commit-fanout.log (entries show nonmonotonic commit indices).
- Edge metrics: routing_snapshot_version divergence observed on ep-us-east-b (version 128 vs 129 on other edges).
- Traces: trace IDs provided below show mixed-variant calls: [trace: 2f3a1b8c, trace: 2f3a1bd0].

Temporary mitigations performed:
- 2026-03-11T10:40Z - Applied tenant-level explicit pin to redwood-v2-3b-alpha (pin API) to lock cohort until control-plane fully converged.
- 2026-03-11T10:45Z - Restarted ep-us-east-b to force snapshot resync.
- 2026-03-11T11:05Z - Orchestrator rolling resync invoked to reconcile commit index.

Current status:
- Immediate customer impact mitigated by explicit pin and edge restart.
- Root-cause investigation underway; incident declared in #support-ops Slack and tracking in this ticket.

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis 1: Staggered application of weight changes due to race in staged-commit path; control-plane replicas accept commits without a quorum check for the updated routing snapshot sequence.
- Hypothesis 2: Edge snapshot ingestion code tolerates out-of-order commit indices and applies older snapshots when they arrive later, causing temporary divergence.
- Evidence: Orchestrator logs show commit index 129 applied, then 128 applied on replica B within ~7s, followed by snapshot push to ep-us-east-b.
- Corroborating data: ep-us-east-b routing_snapshot_version metric lagged by one version for the duration of the window.

Suggested immediate fixes and follow-ups:
- Short term: Add a control-plane guard to reject commits with lower/equal sequence numbers than the last-applied sequence on that replica (hotfix).
- Medium term: Implement quorum-based commit confirmation for staged weight changes and add monotonic routing_snapshot_version that edges strictly validate.
- Long term: Add integration test that simulates partial replica lag and asserts snapshot monotonicity across edges.

Follow-ups assigned to eng teams after triage:
- Orchestrator: review staged-commit logic (owner: eng/orchestrator).
- Edge: stricter snapshot version validation and resync backoff (owner: eng/edge).
- SRE: add alert for control-plane commit-index divergence across replicas.
comments: 2026-03-11T10:38Z - Support (Sofia Martinez): Customer reports mixed responses within same chat session. Collected sample session IDs and traces; escalating to SRE.
2026-03-11T10:44Z - SRE (Arun Patel): Applied tenant pin and restarted ep-us-east-b. Early telemetry suggests fallback rate dropping. Investigating control-plane commit logs.
2026-03-11T11:20Z - Product (Lina Zhou): Noted that operator used the web console to apply incremental weights via UI. Need to confirm console action sequence and possible client-side retry behavior.
notes: Post-incident actions: schedule postmortem if root-cause confirmed; update runbook to require quorum confirmation on staged rollouts; notify customer of findings and compensatory credits if requested.
